key_facts.fact: The owner's single most-repeated requirement is emotional, relational, exactly-human-sounding voice. It appears 7 times across 10-17, 10-18, 10-19, 10-20 (x3) and 10-21, and the owner calls it 'the main thing'.
The owner explicitly ranks the voice above margin: margin may be compromised, the voice may not.

The owner defines world-class telecalling as: open with something interesting, never waste their time, read the person, talk more if they want, ask clearly, get the agenda done subtly. Opening with 'I am an AI agent' and repeating it makes people hang up.
The application must be LLM-native: the client talks to VP's agent, which explains and does the setup and campaign, rather than navigating a fixed structure ('he just have to talk').
Chat-driven setup alone is parity, not a wedge: 5 of 6 walked dashboards ship a copilot, among them ElevenLabs Architect and Bolna Auto Build.

Price target is about Rs 2/min or under, 'missing nothing', repeated 5 times. Measured evidence says Gemini Live cannot hit it (Rs 4.2-5.7/min at 3-minute calls), and per-minute launch pricing modelled at -47% to +1% margin.

Self-learning (call 100's drop-off line rewritten on call 101, 'on the go self improvement in every way') is stated 3 times. The owner sequences it after v1, behind memory and personalisation, on harness2 fundamentals.

Naive self-learning is measurably unsafe: daily-checked K=2 A/B dashboards gave 52-62% false winners in A/A by day 90, and cross-tenant pooled learning gave the wrong winner to 48-55% of dissimilar tenants.
The owner wants users to choose STT, brain and TTS (and the copilot's overall brain), with 4-5 curated combinations. The owner leans to Gemini TTS and Gemini STT.

Round 1: every stack's conversation was robotic; the best stack was Gemini 3.1 Live at 7.0/10. Brief v2 cut words per turn from 33 to 20 and abrupt hang-ups from 17-40% to 0, but human round 2 has not run.
Turn-taking is unsolved across all stacks: 15-42% cut-ins.

The owner has rejected the product's look and flow three times: the /prototype (2026-09-22), the whole Relay design and usability (2026-10-01), and the Codex baseline as 'very basic and stale' (2026-10-15).

Feature parity plus a price undercut was rejected as a wedge. Incumbents ship 10-12 of 12 headline features; Indian all-in list prices are Rs 3.5-7/min. The owner's 'parity made better' must be a floor, with the wedge on measured task failures.
All six walked dashboards lack consent, DND and DLT on the campaign form, a predicted reply gap and a Hinglish mode, and none reached a ring on an Indian line.

The owner never raised TRAI, DND, DLT or consent. Compliance requirements in the blueprint come from research, not owner messages; disclosure comes from the standing rule and a 2026-09-22 Relay-era user clarification.

The owner's regional-dialect wish (Bihari-Hindi mix) conflicts with research: employers ask for a dialect in 1 of 828 Hindi-belt postings, and no dialect TTS locale exists. It fits as a personalisation feature, not a wedge.
The owner wants VP to keep learning from competitors always, including new launches, and to store all knowledge so no effort or tokens are wasted (each stated 3-4 times).
Onboarding target is 30-60 minutes self-serve: any data in, fire an agent, every recording, overview plus deep analytics.
Pre-sale vs post-sale was demoted by the owner to a go-to-market input. Research separately rejected cold outbound sales as the lead job under TRAI.
